transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well... I guess I'm just here because I've been forgetting things. Important things, I suppose. Like... I missed a follow-up for my heart recently. And I forget to call the clinic back. Or, you know, I'll go to fix something around the house and realize I didn't bring the right tools. Just stuff like that.
Are these memory problems making it hard for you to manage your usual day-to-day tasks on your own?

I suppose it is. The, uh... the repair group down at the senior center, they can't really count on me the way they used to. And... well, like I mentioned, my doctor's office keeps having to chase me down about those missed heart follow-ups. So... yeah. I guess it gets in the way.
Have your memory problems been slowly getting worse over time?
I'm not really sure. I haven't paid that much attention to it, to be honest. It's just... I notice it more now, I guess.
Because of these memory problems, do you need help from someone else to manage your daily life?
No... I don't think so. I still do things for myself. I mean, I get by alright on my own. I don't have anybody doing things for me, if that's what you're asking.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
No... I wouldn't say that. I feel fine in that department. Just... going about my day, you know. I don't really get down like that.
Has anyone close to you told you they’ve noticed your memory getting worse?
No, not really. People don't say much about it to me. I guess they haven't noticed anything worth bringing up.
Is there someone who knows you well that I could ask whether they’ve noticed changes in your memory?
No... I'd rather not. I mostly just keep to myself anyway. There's really no one you need to be calling.
Have you ever been told by a doctor that you have a brain condition or a medical illness that could affect your memory?
No... I haven't. Doctors never said anything like that to me. Just... no, nothing like that.
Have you been feeling unusually worried or anxious lately?
No, not really. I don't... I don't spend much time worrying about things. Just going about my day, mostly. So, no.
Are you having trouble managing your bills?

Bills? No... they get paid. It's more... well, I guess what actually brought me in is I just keep forgetting things I really shouldn't. Like... my heart follow-up appointments. Or I'll forget to call the clinic back. Even just... going to do a repair job and realizing I didn't bring the right tools. Just... things like that.
Because of your memory, have you needed help keeping track of your medications?
No... I handle my own pills. I don't need anybody helping me with that. I just... I take them.
Because of your memory, have you gotten lost when going somewhere familiar?
No, I don't get lost. I know my way around just fine.
Compared with a year ago, are you less able to do your usual activities?
No... not really. I still do my usual stuff just fine. It's about the same.
Have you ever taken a memory or thinking test with a doctor?
No... I haven't done anything like that. Never had a reason to.
Would you be willing to do a brief memory and thinking test today?
I suppose so... if you think we need to. I don't mind.
On a brief memory and thinking test today, did you have trouble?
Not that I noticed. Seemed fine to me.
Did the doctor tell you that you scored below normal on the memory test today?
No... nobody said anything like that to me.
Did the doctor say your score on today’s memory test was lower than expected for someone your age?
No... like I just said, nobody told me anything about the score. I just took it and that was it.
Did the doctor tell you that your memory or thinking test today showed any problems?
Look... no. I really don't know why you keep asking me the exact same thing. Nobody said there were any problems.
Over the past year, has your memory clearly gotten worse?
No, not really. I haven't noticed anything like that.
